explain.say: The Falkirk Wheel in Scotland is a giant rotating boat lift that joins two canals at different heights. Instead of a long flight of locks, it lifts boats about 24 metres in a single half turn.

faq.q: How does the Falkirk Wheel work?
faq.a: Two water-filled gondolas sit at opposite ends of a giant rotating arm. Boats float in, the wheel turns half a turn, and one gondola rises to the upper canal while the other drops to the lower basin.
asks: How does a rotating boat lift work?

faq.q: Why does a gondola weigh the same with or without a boat?
faq.a: By Archimedes' principle, a floating boat pushes out exactly its own weight of water. As it floats in, that much water flows out, so the gondola's total weight does not change.
asks: Why doesn't the boat make the gondola heavier?

faq.q: Why does the Falkirk Wheel need so little power?
faq.a: The two gondolas always weigh the same and balance each other, so the motors only overcome friction and get the wheel moving; they never lift the weight.
asks: How much energy does the Falkirk Wheel use?

faq.q: How do the gondolas stay level?
faq.a: A set of gears linked to a fixed central gear turns each gondola the opposite way to the arms, so it stays level as they rotate, like the cars on a big wheel.
asks: Why doesn't the water spill out?

faq.q: Why was the Falkirk Wheel built?
faq.a: It reconnected the Forth and Clyde Canal with the Union Canal, which had been linked by a flight of 11 locks that was filled in in the 1930s. The wheel opened in 2002.
asks: When did the Falkirk Wheel open?

facts: The Falkirk Wheel, opened in 2002, lifts boats 24 metres between the Forth and Clyde Canal and the Union Canal.
A floating boat displaces its own weight of water, so a gondola with a boat weighs the same as one without.

quiz.say: A 20-tonne boat floats into one Falkirk Wheel gondola. How does that gondola's total weight change?
quiz.show: A 20-tonne boat floats in. The gondola's weight…
quiz.why: The boat pushes out 20 tonnes of water, which flows out of the gondola, so the total stays the same.

wrong.1: That would be true if no water left, but the floating boat displaces its own weight.
